node: University services and online program management
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the university services and online program management node. The strongest direct exposure is Grand Canyon Education, which is structurally closest to an OPM/service-provider model through long-running university partner support. Strategic Education and Perdoceo are more direct education asset owners and online workforce-learning platforms than outsourced OPM vendors, but they are relevant reference/adjacent operators because they own accredited online postsecondary assets and employer-aligned education channels. Nelnet is a second-order underfollowed infrastructure candidate through campus payments, tuition management, and higher-education technology services rather than enrollment marketing or academic program execution. No buy/sell view is implied. Layer 1B expansion for the university services and OPM node found a small set of US-listed companies tied to the hard-to-replace operating layer behind online, hybrid, workforce, and healthcare education programs. The strongest chokepoint angles are not generic online-course delivery, but institutional trust, regulated enrollment/payment infrastructure, university partner relationships, healthcare program capacity, clinical/simulation infrastructure, and long-duration operating systems that become costly for schools to replace. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Expanded the university services and OPM node with a two-lane universe focused on US-listed small/mid-cap or overlooked education infrastructure names. The cleanest direct exposure is Grand Canyo
